note: POLARITY WARNING -- THIS PREDICATE IS INVERTED RELATIVE TO match.json AND TO THE ISSUE. A `repro` scored under match-export.json means the EXPORT half of #2633's request IS PRESENT, not that the issue reproduces. `bisect --match match-export.json` therefore reports a `regressed-in <tag>` line whose real meaning is `the capability APPEARED in <tag>`. It is written this way on purpose: the natural spelling (`not_contains OpCapability Linkage`) is an absence predicate, and SKILL.md step 6 records that an absence clause is satisfied for FREE by any release that fails to compile the repro for an unrelated reason -- which is precisely what the oldest releases here do. A positive clause cannot be satisfied by a compile that never ran. WHAT IT MEASURES: cmd.txt line 2 compiles lib-export.hlsl, an `export`-qualified function with no entry point, at the DEFAULT target env. A build that generates SPIR-V linkage emits `OpCapability Linkage`, and the text is observable in both of the two shapes that produces -- (a) as a line of a successfully disassembled module, and (b) echoed back by dxc's own SPIR-V validator, which at the default Vulkan env rejects it: `fatal error: generated SPIR-V is invalid: Capability Linkage is not allowed by Vulkan 1.0 specification (or requires extension)` followed by `  OpCapability Linkage`. Measured on main-debug (ab5400907): shape (b), exit 0x80004005. CONTROLS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, all captured, because a predicate that reads a validator echo is exactly the #3092 trap and has to be shown to discriminate: (1) variant-export-universal15-* runs the SAME source with -fspv-target-env=universal1.5, which compiles clean to shape (a) -- --expect match, proving the predicate is not merely reading an error message; (2) control-defined.hlsl compiles cleanly with NO `export` qualifier -- --expect no-match, proving the predicate does not fire on any successful lib_6_3 SPIR-V compile; (3) the primary capture's line 1 (repro.hlsl) fails with a diagnostic and contributes no match, so a failed compile does not satisfy it. Source anchor: DeclResultIdMapper.cpp:1824 calls spvBuilder.decorateLinkage(..., LinkageType::Export) for any FunctionDecl carrying HLSLExportAttr; CapabilityVisitor.cpp:411 turns that decoration into Capability Linkage. There is no LinkageType::Import call site anywhere in tools/clang/lib/SPIRV, which is the asymmetry the two predicates measure.
